program_name: Fashion Communication and Luxury Strategies (Master's Degree Course in Fashion Communication and Luxury Strategies). There is no separate Italian-named twin course: the Italian-language site lists the programme under "Corsi di Laurea Magistrale" with the identical English name "Fashion Communication and Luxury Strategies", and the programme page's own "Course Name" and "Course Name in English" fields are both "Fashion Communication and Luxury Strategies". Unlike three other IULM master's courses (Art, Valorization Strategies and the Market; Hospitality and Tourism Management; Strategic Communication) it is NOT branded as a "Dual Degree" course.
teaching_language: Fully English-taught. The programme page states "The programme, taught entirely in English, includes a common first year" and "The course is delivered in English"; the Course information block gives "Language in which the course is taught: English", and the apply.iulm.it record gives "Study language: English". There is no Italian-taught component of the curriculum, and no Italian twin course. However, the admission regulations impose a separate Italian-language obligation that is NOT an entry condition but a graduation condition: candidates who are not native Italian speakers and/or non-Italian citizens must declare their Italian level when applying for the admission test and must obtain, by the end of their studies, a qualification attesting to written and oral proficiency in Italian.
campus: Milan (Milano) - IULM single campus, Via Carlo Bo 1, 20143 Milano. The programme page gives "Academic venue: Milan"; apply.iulm.it gives "Study location: Italy, Milan". Faculty of Arts, Fashion and Tourism.
degree_class: LM-92 - Teorie della comunicazione, rendered on the English programme page simply as "Degree Class: LM-92" and in the English admission regulations as "LM-92 Theories of Communication". Ordering: D.M. 270/2004. 120 ECTS over 2 years.
academic_requirements:
PLACES: 100 places for a.y. 2026/2027 ("1. Number of places available for the academic year 2026/2027 - 100 places"). The general master's enrolment page tabulates "Fashion Communication and Luxury Strategies - 100 (limited places)". The Italian-language registration page shows the identical figure ("posti disponibili 100"), so there is NO quota discrepancy between the English and Italian pages for this programme. The programme page classifies access as a "Course with planned number of places with selective knowledge testing".

PRIOR QUALIFICATION: A first-cycle (Bachelor's) university degree, awarded or about to be awarded, with graduation before the autumn session of a.y. 2025/26, i.e. before 31 December 2026. apply.iulm.it states the entry qualification as "Bachelor's degree. Applicants' academic credentials will be evaluated on a case-by-case basis, provided they expect to graduate by December 31st, 2026." The general IULM international prerequisites page requires "a relevant and coherent Bachelor's degree diploma correspondent to EQF (European Qualification Framework) Level 6 and 180 ECTS or more", plus "adequate Italian/English language proficiency" and "specific basic knowledge about core subjects".

CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS (route 1 - degree class): the Bachelor's degree must belong to one of the Italian classes L-1 (Cultural heritage), L-3 (Visual arts, music, performing arts and fashion), L-4 (Industrial design), L-5 (Philosophy), L-10 (Arts), L-11 (Modern languages and cultures), L-12 (Language mediation), L-15 (Tourism), L-18 (Economics and corporate management), L-20 (Communication), L-24 (Psychology), L-31 (Information technology), L-40 (Sociology), or an equivalent foreign degree qualification.

CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS (route 2 - credits): candidates graduating in any other class must have acquired at least 60 CFU/ECTS (in the Bachelor's degree, via single university courses, or via a university master's degree) by the application deadline, structured as: (a) at least 18 CFU in L-ART/03, L-ART/05, L-ART/06, L-ART/07; (b) at least 12 CFU in SECS-P/01, SECS-P/02, SECS-P/04, SECS-P/07, SECS-P/08, SECS-P/10, SECS-P/12; (c) at least 6 CFU in ICAR/13, ICAR/17; and the remainder collectively in INF/01, ING-INF/01; L-FIL-LET/10, L-FIL-LET/11, L-FIL-LET/14; L-LIN/01, L-LIN/03, L-LIN/04, L-LIN/10, L-LIN/11, L-LIN/12; SPS/02, SPS/04, SPS/07, SPS/08, SPS/09; M-PSI/01, M-PSI/05, M-PSI/06; M-FIL/01, M-FIL/03, M-FIL/04, M-FIL/05; M-DEA/01; M-STO/02, M-STO/04, M-STO/05, M-STO/06.

AFAM / SSML APPLICANTS: unlike Strategic Communication (which excludes AFAM graduates outright), this programme assesses them individually - "Applications from students or graduates from AFAM Institutes ... or SSML Institutes ... will be assessed on an individual basis considering the applicants' study plans". Such applicants must e-mail a detailed exam certificate to ammissioni.magistrali@iulm.it BEFORE applying online, and may apply online only after approval by the Coordinator for Master's Degree Courses.

RANKING / SELECTION CRITERIA - three distinct candidate tracks:
(a) INTERNAL graduates/undergraduates (IULM Bachelor's in Fashion and Creative Industries / Moda e industrie creative) applying in sessions 1-2 are ranked WITHOUT any test, on average mark rounded to two decimals: session 1 requires at least 90 CFU registered as of 25 November 2025 and an average mark no lower than 26/30, with later verification of 120 CFU as of 15 February 2026 (Annex 1 procedure); session 2 requires at least 120 CFU as of 15 February 2026 and an average no lower than 25/30; graduates in sessions 1-2 need a pre-graduation exam average no lower than 26/30. Internal candidates must also meet the English B2 requirement (no exemption is granted for this programme). "A maximum total of 50 candidates will be admitted to the ranking list." Internal candidates excluded by that 50-place cap, or falling below the merit threshold, take the same test as external candidates under identical criteria. Internal students on first-semester international mobility must e-mail ammissioni.magistrali@iulm.it so that CFU gained abroad and awaiting approval can be counted. "Any changes to the number of places reserved for internal candidates will be announced one week before the date of the test."
(b) EXTERNAL graduates/undergraduates (including Italian citizens holding a foreign qualification obtained in Italy or abroad): admission is by admission test score plus merit points. Merit points on Bachelor's degree grade: up to 88/110 = 0 points; 89-98/110 = 1 point; 99-110/110 = 2 points; 110/110 cum laude = 3 points. For undergraduates, merit points come from the registered exam average instead: up to and including 25.99/30 = 0; 26/30-27.99/30 = 1; 28/30-29.99/30 = 2; 30/30 = 3. CFU thresholds for external undergraduates: at least 90 CFU as of 25 November 2025 (session 1, with later verification of 120 CFU as of 15 February 2026); 120 CFU as of 15 February 2026 (session 2); 130 CFU as of 23 April 2026 (session 3); 130 CFU as of 18 June 2026 (session 4). SCORE THRESHOLDS (published explicitly for this programme): "Candidates with an overall score (test score + merit points) greater than or equal to 23 will be considered admitted." Candidates scoring 18 or more but under 23 go on a waiting list drawn up in the last available admission test session when places are about to run out. "Candidates with an overall score (test score + merit points) of less than 18 will be declared ineligible"; they may request to apply in a later session via the Registrar's Office. Ranking is on the overall score rounded to two decimals; tie-break order: merit points from the degree mark / average marks at the session's application closing date, then the higher score on the English-language test questions, then the date (and time of payment) the application was submitted. "A maximum of 50 candidates in total will be admitted to the ranking list in the first two sessions." Places unused by the internal quota may be reallocated to the external quota, with changes announced one week before the test date. A candidate may always retake the test in a following session (cancelling the previous score) or carry the previous score forward onto a later ranking list, but only if that score is at least 18.
(c) FOREIGN graduates/undergraduates (EU and/or non-EU) holding a foreign admission qualification obtained in Italy or abroad: after verification of the curricular requirements they sit "an admission test similar to that for candidates with Italian qualifications ... held online". Separate, LOWER thresholds apply: "Candidates with a score of 20 or above will be considered admitted"; scores of 15 or more but under 20 go on a waiting list drawn up in order of ranking until all places are filled; "Candidates with a score of less than 15 will be declared ineligible". Tie-break: higher score on the English-language questions, then application date/time of payment. Note that no merit points are described for this track - foreign candidates are ranked on the raw test score. [uncertain]

ADVANCE (FIRST) SESSION - DOUBLE CFU CHECK (Annex 1): first-session candidates admitted on 90 CFU who enrol by 15 January 2026 must certify 120 CFU as of 15 February 2026. If they cannot, their position is assessed against remaining places: if places are near capacity they lose the place, enrolment is annulled and fees refunded net of statutory charges and a EUR 100 administrative fee; if places are not near capacity they may either forgo enrolment (same refund terms) or defer assessment to the third session, waiving full reimbursement and certifying 130 CFU by 23 April 2026. Failing that at near-capacity, no more than 50% of the fee is reimbursed; otherwise the process repeats for the 4th session on 18 June 2026. "Regardless of the number of CFUs held, after the 4th session if the available places are not filled, the position of these students will be confirmed."

ASSESSMENT OF FOREIGN QUALIFICATIONS: IULM's Admission Office evaluates the documentation submitted on apply.iulm.it, checks the access requirements and confirms eligibility before the admission test (approximately 15 working days after the application fee is paid). At enrolment, holders of a foreign qualification must supply the qualification in the original language with an Italian translation where required, plus authenticity verification - "a Statement of Comparability and/or CIMEA verification, or a Dichiarazione di Valore (official statement issued by the Italian diplomatic authorities), as required by the University". apply.iulm.it accepts entry-qualification documents in English, German, French, Italian or Spanish.

SECOND-YEAR TRACKS: the first year is common to all students; in the second year students choose between "Global Trends" and "Luxury Strategies". Track choice is a curricular decision after enrolment - IULM publishes no separate admission quota, ranking or entry requirement per track.

NO DUAL DEGREE: unlike Strategic Communication, Art/Valorization and Hospitality and Tourism Management, this programme is not marketed as a dual-degree course and no partner-university track or partner-side entry criteria are published.

SPECIAL NEEDS: applicants with disabilities (Law 104/92), Specific Learning Disorders (Law 170/2010), ADHD or Autism must upload valid, legally compliant certification in PDF during the online test enrolment procedure, and must request dispensations/compensatory measures by e-mail to the diversaMENTE service (diversamente@iulm.it, tel. 02.891412200) before the test enrolment deadline.
language_requirements:
ENGLISH - minimum CEFR B2, verified in one of four alternative ways (admission regulations, section 4: "For admission to the Master's Degree Course in Fashion Communication and Luxury Strategies proficiency in English at a level of at least CEFR level B2 is a prerequisite"):
1. A language certificate obtained after 1 January 2024: IELTS with a score of at least 5.5; TOEFL iBT with a score of at least 87; Cambridge English with a score of at least 165.
2. A Bachelor's degree (obtained in Italy or abroad) on a course held in English.
3. Passing IULM's own Assessment Test (Oxford Placement Test), offered online at no extra cost, with a grade of at least level B2 in BOTH the Listening and Use of English sections - so IULM's own placement test fully substitutes for an external certificate.
4. Having already passed the IULM Assessment Test at B2 or above in both sections in an admissions session of a.y. 2025/26, and in any case not before 1 February 2025.
Candidates who do not meet the requirement when registering for the admission test are automatically placed on the Assessment Test list. Assessment Test dates for a.y. 2026/27: 1 December 2025 (session 1); 20 January and 25 February 2026 (session 2); 9 April and 28 April 2026 (session 3, "only if places still available or only for non-EU students"); 27 May 2026 (exceptional session, per the general master's calendar); 25 June 2026 (session 4, "only if places still available or only for non-EU students"); 4 September 2026 (session 5, per the general master's calendar; the programme regulations say only "5th session: dates to be defined only if places still available").
English proficiency is ALSO tested inside the admission test itself: "English language proficiency to at least level B2" is one of the five examined subjects, and the score on the English-language questions is the first tie-break in the ranking.
NO EXEMPTION is published for internal IULM candidates on this programme: "Internal candidates who meet the above requirements must also meet the language requirement, i.e. proficiency in English to at least level B2". (By contrast, Strategic Communication exempts its internal Corporate Communication and Public Relations cohort.)
For international applicants the general international-prerequisites page adds that for an English-taught master's you must submit "an official certificate with a score equal to or higher than level B2 of CEFR ... in compliance with official certificates listed in the Admission Regulations or by passing a English online assessment test".

ITALIAN - not an admission requirement, but a graduation requirement. "Candidates who are not native speakers of Italian and/or non-Italian citizens are required to declare their level of knowledge of the Italian language when applying for the admissions test, and they must obtain by the end of their course of studies the required qualification attesting to written and oral proficiency in Italian." Candidates are directed to the University's separately published "Procedures for the assessment and acquisition of knowledge of the Italian language". The general international-prerequisites page states that a CILS/CELI/PLIDA certificate at CEFR B2, or IULM's online Italian assessment test, is required for ITALIAN-TAUGHT courses; the exact Italian level demanded for graduation from this English-taught course is not stated on any page consulted. IULM offers an intensive Italian language improvement course at the beginning of September. [uncertain]
application_deadline_eu:
Academic year 2026/2027. Applications open 11 November 2025 ("From 11 November 2025, the following categories of candidates will be able to apply for admission following the online procedure"). Registration and payment of the EUR 110 fee is done through my.iulm.it after creating an account.

Six sittings were actually run for this programme (five numbered sessions plus an "exceptional/straordinaria" session). Per session: [application deadline] -> [admission test date] -> [enrolment confirmation deadline]
- Session 1: apply by 25 November 2025 (registration for session 1 opened 11 November 2025 at 10:00 and closed 25 November 2025 at 23:59) -> test 15 December 2025 -> enrol by 15 January 2026.
- Session 2: apply by 19 February 2026 -> test 3 March 2026 -> enrol by 31 March 2026. Merit/CFU documentation deadline for this session: 15 February 2026. Flagged in the regulations as "only if places still available or only for non-EU students".
- Exceptional session ("sessione straordinaria"): test 9 June 2026 -> enrol by 29 June 2026. This session appears only in the general master's calendar, NOT in the programme's own admission regulations, and no application deadline is published for it. [uncertain]
- Session 3: apply by 23 April 2026 -> test 14 May 2026 -> enrol by 4 June 2026. "Only if places still available or only for non-EU students".
- Session 4: apply by 18 June 2026 (the university-wide registration window for the fourth test session opened 22 May 2026 at 10:00 and closed 18 June 2026 at 23:59) -> test 9 July 2026 -> enrol by 28 July 2026. "Only if places still available or only for non-EU students".
- Session 5: registration window 30 June 2026 10:00 - 31 August 2026 23:59 -> test 10 September 2026 -> enrol by 18 September 2026. The programme regulations say only "5th session: dates to be defined only if admissions test is to be held"; the concrete dates come from the general master's enrolment page and the Italian test-dates and deadlines pages.

IMPORTANT - THIS PROGRAMME DID NOT FILL EARLY. Unlike Marketing, Consumer Behaviour and Communication and Strategic Communication, Fashion Communication and Luxury Strategies was never declared sold out. IULM's 25 May 2026 fourth-session news item lists a session-4 test date for it ("Fashion Communication and Luxury Strategies: July 9, 2026") while stating that "For Marketing, Consumer Behaviour and Communication (English language course) and Strategic Communication, seats are sold out." The general master's enrolment page, as displayed for the fifth session, still shows "Fashion Communication and Luxury Strategies - 100 (limited places)" while marking Marketing and Strategic Communication as "available places have been filled out", and it schedules a fifth Fashion test on 10 September 2026. So all sessions through session 5 were usable for this programme.

Other notes: "Deadlines for sessions after the first are to be checked subject to availability of places." "Depending on the number of admissions and the number of remaining places, the deadlines for enrolments may be shortened to allow the scrolling of the ranking list." Candidates who fail one session may re-apply for a later session without paying the EUR 110 fee again, subject to availability of places. Enrolment is confirmed only on payment of the first instalment. Candidates without a degree certificate yet are enrolled "conditionally" and must communicate the degree date and grade and upload the certificate no later than 31 December 2026, failing which the enrolment is annulled with no refund of the first instalment or the test fee. Internal IULM third-year students applying in session 2 have their a.y. 2025/26 third-instalment deadline deferred from 31 March to 22 April 2026. Teaching for a.y. 2026/27 starts 21 September 2026.
application_deadline_non_eu:
Non-EU applicants residing abroad apply through the dedicated international platform apply.iulm.it (DreamApply), not through the standard my.iulm.it Italian online procedure. The international procedure page states: "Non-EU applicants living abroad can submit their application on apply.iulm.it, subject to availability of places for the two-year master degree course in which they are interested, by the end of April." So the effective non-EU application cut-off for a.y. 2026/2027 was the end of April 2026.

Steps: (1) submit the application on apply.iulm.it with all required documents for an assessment of qualifications; (2) pay the application fee (apply.iulm.it lists "Application fee EUR 60 one-time"; the IULM admission regulations separately set the admission test fee at EUR 110); (3) evaluation of documents and assessment of eligibility - "our team will review your application and get back to you within approximately 15 working days, confirming that you meet the access requirements and informing you about the admission test date"; (4) sit the online admission test (for foreign-qualification holders, a test "similar to that for candidates with Italian qualifications", passed at a score of 20 or above); (5) enrol via the University's Online Services; (6) pay the first instalment of tuition fees to reserve the place.

LATE SESSIONS FAVOUR NON-EU APPLICANTS: sessions 2, 3 and 4 are expressly flagged in the admission regulations as running "only if places still available or only for non-EU students", so the later sittings are reserved primarily for non-EU candidates. Because this programme was not sold out, non-EU candidates retained access through the 10 September 2026 fifth session.

VISA / PRE-ENROLMENT: admitted non-EU students must lodge the pre-enrolment request for a study visa with the Italian consular authorities. IULM instructs applicants to "Submit a student visa application via Universitaly platform from March to the end of May", and the apply.iulm.it course record adds: "Admitted students must submit pre-enrolment request for student visa to the Italian consular authorities. For more details on the procedure and any updates, visit: www.universitaly.it/studenti-stranieri".

FINAL ENROLMENT CUT-OFF FOR FOREIGN-QUALIFICATION HOLDERS: "Students holding a foreign qualification are required to complete the enrolment process no later than 31 January 2027 by submitting all documentation required for this purpose, including: a Type D study visa (where required); their tax code (codice fiscale); the admission qualification in the original language together with an Italian translation (where required); and documentation verifying the authenticity of the qualification, such as a Statement of Comparability and/or CIMEA verification, or a Dichiarazione di Valore." Failure to comply by 31 January 2027 annuls the 2026/27 enrolment ex officio with no entitlement to a refund of fees already paid.

REFUNDS: the first instalment is non-refundable, with one exception - "The only exception is represented by student visa denial from the Italian Embassy or Consulate in the country of residence for non-EU applicants."

STATUS AS AT 6 SEPTEMBER 2026: apply.iulm.it displays "Apply now! Academic year 2026/27 - Application period has ended - Studies commence 21 Sept 2026". Critically, and unlike the Strategic Communication and Comunicazione d'Impresa records, the Fashion record carries NO "we reached full capacity for this programme" note - the window simply closed as scheduled.

entry_exam_or_test:
Restricted-access programme with a selective written admission test. Fee: EUR 110, "not refundable under any circumstances (with the exception of failure to take the test due to the exhaustion of available places or at the behest of the University's governing bodies)". All candidates must apply and pay, including those admitted directly (i.e. the internal no-test track). Non-payment, or payment after the session deadline, precludes admission to the test.

SUBJECTS TESTED: "The admission test is aimed at ascertaining the candidates' knowledge in the following subjects: history of fashion and design; history of contemporary art; digital marketing; practical IT activities; English language proficiency to at least level B2."

FORMAT AND DURATION: "It consists of a written test in English comprising 44 multiple-choice questions. In addition, there are 16 further questions aimed at testing the candidate's skills in the following areas and which do not count towards the final mark for the purposes of the ranking: text comprehension, logic, numerical and verbal reasoning. There are no penalties in the event of an omitted or incorrect answer. A maximum time limit of 50 minutes is allowed for answering the 60 questions." "The tests will be carried out online." There is NO interview or oral stage for this programme (unlike Hospitality and Tourism Management, which runs a two-stage written plus oral test).

RECOMMENDED BIBLIOGRAPHY (published in the regulations, to be studied together with an English language textbook at B2 or above):
- Digital marketing: David Chaffey, Digital Marketing, London, Pearson, 2019.
- History of contemporary art: H.E. Read, A Concise History of Modern Painting, Thames & Hudson, London, 1974.
- History of design: Domitilla Dardi & Vanni Pasca, Design History Handbook, Cinisello Balsamo, Silvana Editoriale, 2019.
- History of fashion: Rebecca Arnold, Fashion. A Very Short Introduction, Oxford University Press, 2009; Valerie Mendes & Amy de la Haye, Fashion Since 1900, London, Thames & Hudson, 2021.
- Also recommended: Yuniya Kawamura, Fashion-ology. Fashion Studies in the Postmodern Digital Era, London, Bloomsbury, 2023.
- Basic IT: D. Curtin, K. Foley, K. Sen, C. Morin, Informatica di base, 6th edition, 2016, McGraw-Hill. (Note: this recommended IT text is in Italian even though the test itself is in English.)

SCORING AND PASS MARKS: the raw test score is combined with merit points (0-3) from the Bachelor's degree grade (graduates) or registered exam average (undergraduates). For candidates with an Italian qualification: overall score (test + merit) of 23 or above = admitted; 18 to under 23 = waiting list drawn up in the last available session when places are about to run out; under 18 = ineligible (may request a later session via the Registrar's Office). For holders of a FOREIGN qualification, sitting a similar online test, the thresholds are lower: 20 or above = admitted; 15 to under 20 = waiting list; under 15 = ineligible. Tie-breaks: merit points, then the higher score on the English-language questions, then the date and time of application/payment.

PRELIMINARY ENGLISH TEST: candidates without an accepted B2 certificate or an English-taught Bachelor's are automatically scheduled for the free online Assessment Test (Oxford Placement Test), which must be passed at B2 or above in both the Listening and Use of English sections. Dates: 1 Dec 2025; 20 Jan and 25 Feb 2026; 9 Apr and 28 Apr 2026; 27 May 2026 (exceptional session); 25 Jun 2026; 4 Sep 2026.

ADMISSION TEST DATES FOR FASHION COMMUNICATION AND LUXURY STRATEGIES, a.y. 2026/2027 (from the university-wide master's test calendar, which is the most complete source): session 1 - 15 December 2025; session 2 - 3 March 2026; session 3 - 14 May 2026; exceptional session - 9 June 2026; session 4 - 9 July 2026; session 5 - 10 September 2026. Sessions 2, 3 and 4 are qualified in the programme regulations as running "only if places still available or only for non-EU students", and the fifth session date was originally left "to be defined". "The dates of the tests already scheduled are subject to changes, which will be communicated to the candidates in advance." Results are communicated within five working days of the test.

RETAKES: "Students who fail to pass the test in one session may apply for a subsequent session, using the online procedure, without having to pay a further test enrolment fee, subject to verification of the availability of places." A candidate may either retake the test (cancelling the previous score) or carry a previous score of 18 or more onto a later ranking list.

uncertainty_notes:
YEAR COVERED: All figures are for academic year 2026/2027, taken from the English-language admission regulations "Modalita ammissione LM FASHION 2026_2027_ENG.pdf" (Faculty Board meeting 13/10/2025, revised Faculty Board meeting 3/3/2026), the general master's enrolment pages, and the 2026/2027 tuition regulations (Rector's Decree no. 21472 of 27 November 2025). No 2025/2026 fallback was needed for any field.

PROGRAMME NOT REPORTED FULL OR CLOSED BEFORE THE FINAL SESSION - the opposite of Strategic Communication and Marketing, Consumer Behaviour and Communication. Three independent IULM sources confirm this: (1) the 25 May 2026 fourth-session news item names Marketing and Strategic Communication as sold out but lists a live Fashion test date of 9 July 2026; (2) the general master's enrolment page, as displayed for the fifth session, tabulates "Fashion Communication and Luxury Strategies 100 (limited places)" while marking Marketing (Italian and English) and Strategic Communication as "available places have been filled out" and Television, Cinema and New Media as "limited places about to run out"; (3) the apply.iulm.it record for this programme shows only "Application period has ended" with NO "we reached full capacity for this programme" note, whereas the Strategic Communication and Comunicazione d'Impresa records carry exactly that note. A fifth admission test on 10 September 2026 was scheduled and the corresponding registration window (30 June - 31 August 2026) was opened. So all sessions through session 5 were usable. That said, the phrase "limited places" and the regulations' repeated "only if places still available" caveat mean applicants should still treat the November-to-February window (sessions 1-2) as the safe one.

NO QUOTA DISCREPANCY BETWEEN LANGUAGE VERSIONS - explicitly checked because it has occurred for other IULM programmes in this research. The English registration page, the Italian registration page and the English admission regulations all state 100 places, and the general master's enrolment table agrees. Verified by fetching the raw HTML of both /en/.../iscrizioni and /it/.../iscrizioni.

SESSION-4 TEST DATE CONTRADICTION BETWEEN PAGES. The countdown widget at the top of BOTH the English and the Italian registration pages reads "3rd session 14/05/26 - 4th session 25/06/26 - test dates extra session 10/09/26". This is wrong or at least misleading in two ways: 25 June 2026 is the ENGLISH ASSESSMENT TEST date for session 4, not the admission test, which the admission regulations, the news item of 25 May 2026 and the university-wide test calendar all put at 9 July 2026; and the "extra session" of 10 September 2026 is in fact the FIFTH session, while the genuine exceptional/straordinaria session was 9 June 2026. The widget also omits sessions 1 and 2 and the 9 June exceptional sitting. The admission regulations PDF plus the general master's enrolment page were treated as authoritative over the widget.

EXCEPTIONAL SESSION NOT IN THE PROGRAMME REGULATIONS. The "exceptional session" (Italian "sessione straordinaria") with test on 9 June 2026 and enrolment by 29 June 2026 appears only in the university-wide master's calendar and deadlines pages, not in this programme's own admission regulations, which list five numbered sessions. No application/registration deadline for the exceptional session is published on any page consulted; the CFU-certification and merit-documentation deadlines listed in the regulations likewise cover only sessions 1-4. Similarly, the regulations say "5th session: dates to be defined only if admissions test is to be held", and the concrete session-5 dates (test 10 September 2026, enrolment by 18 September 2026, registration 30 June - 31 August 2026) had to be taken from the general pages.

FOREIGN-QUALIFICATION TRACK - MERIT POINTS UNCLEAR. For candidates with an Italian qualification the regulations combine a test score with 0-3 merit points and set a pass at 23. For holders of a foreign admission qualification the text speaks only of "a score", with a pass at 20, waiting list from 15, ineligible below 15, and does not say whether merit points from the foreign degree grade are added or whether 20 is a raw test score on the same scale. The regulations also describe the foreign-candidate test only as "an admission test similar to that for candidates with Italian qualifications" without confirming that it is the identical 44+16-question, 50-minute paper; and unlike Strategic Communication there is no separate written case-study format for this track. The link to "the dates of which are published at the following link" in that paragraph is not resolvable from the extracted PDF text. Prospective international applicants should confirm with admission@iulm.it / ammissioni.magistrali@iulm.it.

ITALIAN-LANGUAGE GRADUATION REQUIREMENT NOT QUANTIFIED. The regulations require non-native-Italian speakers to obtain "by the end of their course of studies the required qualification attesting to written and oral proficiency in Italian" and refer to a separate document, "Procedures for the assessment and acquisition of knowledge of the Italian language", which was not retrieved. The CEFR level and the accepted certificates for that graduation requirement are therefore unknown; the B2 CILS/CELI/PLIDA standard on the general international-prerequisites page applies expressly to Italian-taught programmes.

SECOND-YEAR TRACK NAMING INCONSISTENCY ON THE PROGRAMME PAGE. The "Areas of study" section names the second-year curricula "Global Trends" and "Luxury Strategies", while the "Learning objectives" section on the same page names them "Global Trends" and "Luxury Fashion". apply.iulm.it and the programme title support "Luxury Strategies", which is used here. IULM publishes no separate admission quota, ranking or entry requirement per track, and does not state when or how the track is chosen.

FEE FIGURES AND STALE FEE LINKS ON THE ENGLISH PAGE. The tuition_or_fees_link PDF applies to students whose family resides abroad (single contribution band): EUR 10,806 total for a first-year master's student (EUR 2,000 first instalment + EUR 146 regional tax advance on enrolment, EUR 5,300 + EUR 60 due by 14/12/2026, EUR 3,300 due by 31/03/2027), matching the EUR 10,806 shown on apply.iulm.it. Annex 1 of the fee regulations lists Developing Countries under Ministerial Decree no. 166/2025 for whom a reduced band applies, but the exact reduced amount was not extracted here. Students assessed on an Italian ISEE pay according to the separate general fee regulations. NOTE a document-currency defect: the ENGLISH registration page still links the 2025/2026 fee regulations ("IULM - Regolamento Tasse AA 2025-2026.pdf") and the 2025/26 fee summary, while the ITALIAN registration page correctly links the 2026/2027 regulations ("Regolamento Tasse AA 2026-2027-compresso.pdf"). The 2026/2027 summary cited here was reached from the general fees area, not from the programme page.

OTHER. Faculty naming is inconsistent on the programme page itself: the "Course information" block says "Faculty: Arts and Tourism" while the registration page header and apply.iulm.it both say "Faculty of Arts, Fashion and Tourism". The apply.iulm.it page returns HTTP 403 to WebFetch and was read via a direct HTTP request instead; its content is quoted as displayed on 6 September 2026, at which point the 2026/27 application period had closed. No programme-specific scholarship or fee-waiver page is linked from the Fashion pages. Unlike Strategic Communication, this programme has no dual-degree route and no 50%-reduced remote-test fee or Recruiting-Agent waiver is mentioned in its regulations.
